defects_found: The chrome overflowed the page at 320 px with a long workspace name: .collab-switcher and .collab-account are flex items and default to min-width auto, so the context name could not shrink and its ellipsis never applied. CF-P7-012 could not see it because it qualified the switcher on its own, with no flex parent to refuse; the composed chrome is the only place it appears.

blocked_on.owner_action: Decide whether functions/_lib/identity/environment.ts line 67 or the Pages Preview COLLABORATION_ENABLED value is the bug, so CF-P7-017 can dispatch the API shell; then rebuild codex-cf-p3-preview and drive the signed-in journeys, which no agent can do because obtaining an OAuth session means entering credentials at github.com.
blocked_on.reason: Re-measured 2026-07-27. The originally recorded blocker -- COLLABORATION_ENABLED not set for the Preview environment -- has been cleared by the owner and IT CHANGED NOTHING ON THE WIRE. /api/v1/session on the codex-cf-p3-preview alias and /api/v1/session and /api/v1/workspaces on production all still answer 503 COLLABORATION_UNAVAILABLE. The cause is in the code: functions/_lib/api-shell.mjs lines 285-293 compute hasReviewedDisabledState and then return the identical 503 on BOTH branches, so no value of the flag can make any /api/v1/* route answer anything else. That is CF-P7-017, which is OPEN and blocked on an owner decision because functions/_lib/identity/environment.ts line 67 reads the same flag with the opposite polarity to its name. A third reason survives both: the journeys to be qualified are signed-in journeys and no OAuth session is available to an agent, so qualifying this story is owner-driven regardless.
blocked_on.owner_action_taken_and_insufficient: COLLABORATION_ENABLED='true' was set for the Pages Preview environment and D-P7-01 is executed in wrangler.jsonc. Necessary, and not sufficient.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: an unlock secret to protect the device key
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: DeviceKeyLifecycle.enroll takes an unlock secret, and the passphrase surface that would collect one is not among the twelve CF-P7-001 froze. Adding it is a contract change under its own story, not an implementation detail of this one.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: a client-side workspace-DEK sealer, and an active device to seal to
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: runCreateWorkspace needs keys.sealCreatorEnvelope, which exists nowhere in the browser: Phase 5 shipped the device key pair and the server-side envelope services, and Phase 6 drove the sealing by hand. Writing one here would be a new cryptographic primitive, which the Phase 7 governing principle forbids. The surface states the nearer half of the reason itself -- there is no active device -- and holds its submit control disabled rather than failing on press.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: an active device to bind the membership to
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: InvitationAcceptRequest carries a device id, and device registration is unavailable for the reason above. The review half is composed and reads live: the token is taken from the fragment, the address bar is cleared by replacement, and the invitation is described. Only the final accept is held, with the surface stating why.

A conflict is raised by a document mutation, and no document surface exists in the frozen Phase 7 inventory -- the handoff scoped the document experience but CF-P7-001 froze twelve surfaces without one. The dialog composes and renders its own no-conflict state; it cannot be reached by a user in this build.

journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.missing: a CSRF-exempt path through the API client
journeys_not_completable_in_this_build.reason: POST /api/v1/oauth/github/transactions is public and CSRF-exempt, and the CF-P7-015 client requires a CSRF token on every mutation -- a refusal its own gate proves. Carving an exemption into it is a change to that client under its own review. The control CF-P7-015 shipped on the unauthorized state is therefore not wired here.

declared_limits.sync_reason: Saving, Offline, and Conflict are all derived from outbox entries for an open document, and there is no document surface in the frozen inventory to create one. Saved and Access removed do not need one: Saved is the empty queue, and Access removed is reached from a real workspace-scoped denial followed by a membership re-check, which this build performs.
